kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer applies an `AWSPCAClusterIssuer` custom resource, but that CRD is only installed by the cert-manager / aws-privateca-issuer Helm add-ons created in module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons. The manifest currently depends only on the EKS cluster (module.eks_blueprints) and the CA, so it can be applied before the CRD exists and fail. It should depend on module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (as example_pca_certificate already correctly does). No data reference is possible since that module exposes no outputs.

Per the example's own comments, an ACM PCA Certificate Authority cannot issue certificates until aws_acmpca_certificate_authority_certificate.example installs its root certificate (activation). kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer represents that CA (AWSPCAClusterIssuer) and only references aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.example.arn, so it (and the downstream Certificate) can be created before the CA is activated. It should depend on aws_acmpca_certificate_authority_certificate.example. There is no clean attribute to reference in the issuer manifest (only the CA ARN is used), so a depends_on is the appropriate fix.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already implicitly depends on aws_iam_role.managed_ng through node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn. Listing aws_iam_role.managed_ng again in its depends_on is redundant. (The aws_iam_instance_profile and aws_iam_role_policy_attachment entries in depends_on are not otherwise referenced and should stay.)

null_resource.update_trust_policy already implicitly depends on aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution because its local-exec command interpolates ${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}. Listing it again in depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_trust_policy already implicitly depends on kubernetes_namespace.spark because its local-exec command interpolates ${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}. Listing it again in depends_on is redundant.
